title: Her role with the Harris show and the clowning of the jazz-band era
summary: She played for the show, danced when a chorus girl was short, and did comic piano tricks like playing with a sheet over the keys; the 1920s combos clowned a lot.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When you went out with the Harris show were you just part of the band or did you have a special spot of your own?

No, no special, all I did was I played for the show and when they were short a chorus girl I'd go up on the stage and dance. I never did a solo but we did a combo. You know that was during the era in the 20's of the jazz band, you know, small combos and all they did was clown. A lot of music was coming out of the horns but there was a lot of clowning. That was the jazz band era...
Oh, I'd play music and I'd turn around on the stool... I used to put a sheet over the keys and play with my elbows...
